I follow many different news outlets, ranging from all spectrum's of bias.

As I was looking through The Intercept, I came across this article entitled:

Coast Guard Fired at Migrant Boats, European Border Agency Documents Show

(The actual article is titled "Shoot first," but you only see that once you actually click on the article; otherwise, it's the above title.)

I read through the article because I was curious if this was the U.S. Coast Guard. Considering The Intercept is a U.S. based news outlet that usually talks extensively about U.S. politics, I assumed (and I'm also assuming that was their point,) that they were talking about the United States Coast Guard.

Well, they weren't, they were talking about the Greek Coast Guard.

. . . the passengers start to panic as a Greek coast guard vessel approached them head on

I, obviously, can't say whether or not they were hoping the headline society we live in now would push this story due to the title, but I'm assuming it may have played a part.

Either way, the headline of this article is misleading. I hate when news outlets omit certain important details from their headlines because it will get more clicks. It's dishonest and annoying.

Just wanted to make everyone aware.

TL;DR: It was the Greek Coast Guard, not the U.S. Coast Guard. Just another example of headlines that omit information to drive up clicks.
Keep in mind: The Intercept article about the Coast Guard firing at European boats isn't talking about the U.S. Coast Guard
